format: NIRx continuous-wave (.hdr/.wl1/.wl2), converted to SNIRF for the ecosystem reader
license: openly distributed by MNE-Python for tutorials/examples
record_used: single subject; 8 sources x 16 detectors x 2 wavelengths (760/850 nm) = 56 raw channels -> 28 source-detector pairs after the modified Beer-Lambert law; sampling 7.8125 Hz; ~50 min. Block-design finger-tapping task, three conditions (Control / Tapping_Left / Tapping_Right), 30 blocks each (5 s block duration), read from the recording's own event markers.
pipeline: PhysioNIRS::readSNIRF -> intensityToOD (mean-baseline) -> mbll (modified Beer-Lambert, pathlength factor 6, Scholkmann DPF, the MNE-licensed haemoglobin extinction table) -> nirsActivationGLM (canonical HRF + polynomial drift + AR prewhitening) -> nirsActivationContrast (Tapping - Control, contrast c = [-1, 0.5, 0.5]).
cross_validation: The Beer-Lambert step (mbll) is cross-validated against MNE-Python mne.preprocessing.nirs.beer_lambert_law(ppf=6.0) on the identical data: per-channel HbO and HbR correlation = 1.000000 in all 28 channels; the only difference is the concentration unit (PhysioNIRS uM vs MNE M, a 1e6 scale factor).
note: The MNE dataset ships as NIRx, which MNE reads but cannot write to SNIRF; a SNIRF file was constructed from the intensity + probe geometry + event markers so the recipe uses the ecosystem's own reader (readSNIRF). The grand-average block response is baseline-corrected to the 2 s pre-onset window.
